title: Going Low-Level
summary: Rust below the standard library: calling C and being called from C through the foreign function interface, freestanding no_std programs and a tiny kernel that writes straight to the screen's memory, bare-metal microcontrollers, and how interrupts, exceptions and Unix signals reach a running program.
goals: Match C types and struct layouts with core::ffi and repr(C), and pass strings with CString and CStr
Call C functions, hand C a Rust callback, and wrap a C handle in a safe RAII type
Export Rust functions to C without letting panics cross the boundary
Explain core, alloc and std, and write no_std code against core::fmt::Write and memory-mapped buffers
Describe interrupts, exceptions and signals, and handle a Unix signal with an async-signal-safe handler
